prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (policy-focused, non-ideological; max 500 words)

Fiscal and tax
- Annual deficit cuts, debt falling and current-budget surplus as soon as possible; no new borrowing to fund pledges; OBR auditing of manifestos.
- Savings via zero-based review, digital/government reform; proceeds from bank share sales used to reduce debt; ministerial pay cut/frozen until balance.
- Tax: restore 50p top rate; introduce 10p starting rate funded by ending Marriage Tax Allowance; no rises in basic/higher income tax, NI or VAT; abolish non-dom status; tougher anti-avoidance, HMRC reform; public registries of beneficial ownership in territories.
- Cap structural social security spending.

Economy, industry, infrastructure
- National Infrastructure Commission; support HS2 with cost control; improve northern rail, roads, cycling; swift decision on SE airport capacity.
- Long-term science and innovation funding; decarbonise power by 2030; energy efficiency drive; strengthen Green Investment Bank; Energy Security Board; robust shale regulation; offshore oil strategy.
- Corporate governance: investor duty to long-term growth; tighter takeover rules; stronger public-interest test; transparency and employee voice on top pay.
- Support co-ops/mutuals; retain 30% Royal Mail in public ownership; staff trust for employee shares.
- Small business: create Small Business Administration; cut/freeze business rates for 1.5m small properties; British Investment Bank and regional banks; increase banking competition; levy on payday lenders.

Work, skills, youth
- Minimum Wage >£8 by Oct 2019; promote Living Wage via procurement and first-year tax rebates; pay reporting; enforce underpayment.
- Ban exploitative zero-hours; right to regular contract after 12 weeks; close agency-worker loophole; scrap employment tribunal fees system.
- Apprenticeship guarantee for qualified school leavers; require apprenticeships on major public contracts and for large non-EU skilled hires; focus on Level 3+ and create Technical Degrees; more public-sector apprenticeships.
- Cut university tuition fees to £6,000; curb unpaid internships; Youth Allowance (18–21) tied to training; Compulsory Jobs Guarantee funded by bank bonus tax.

Markets and consumer costs
- Freeze household energy bills until 2017; empower regulator to cut bills; separate generation/supply, open exchanges, simplify tariffs; new watchdog with licence-stripping powers; energy-efficiency loans and standards for private rentals.
- Water: national affordability scheme; stronger regulator.
- Transport: review rail franchising; allow public operator; National Rail body; one-year fare freeze then capped rises; right to cheapest ticket; devolve bus powers and smart ticketing.

Public services, health, care, education
- Fund 8,000 GPs, 20,000 nurses, 3,000 midwives via mansion tax on £2m+ properties, tobacco levy, and anti-avoidance; 48-hour GP access; one-week cancer tests by 2020; integrate physical, mental and social care with personal plans, single coordinator.
- Repeal competition regime in health; cap profits for private clinical providers; mental health parity, 28-day access to talking therapies; public health measures on activity, alcohol, and child-targeted sugar/salt/fat.
- Social care: end 15-minute visits; year-of-care budgets; 5,000 home-care workers; improve carers’ support.
- Education: protect entire education budget; raise technical/vocational route (Technical Baccalaureate; Institutes of Technical Education); English/Maths to 18; independent careers advice; all teachers qualified; leadership development; local Directors of School Standards; cap KS1 classes at 30; require private–state school partnerships; compulsory age-appropriate SRE.

Families, housing, welfare
- Free childcare expanded to 25 hours for working parents of 3–4s; wraparound 8am–6pm childcare via primary schools; double paternity leave/pay.
- Build at least 200,000 homes/year by 2020; first-call for local first-time buyers; Future Homes Fund from Help to Buy ISAs; land transparency and “use it or lose it”; back small builders; garden cities.
- Private renting: three-year tenancies as norm; cap excessive rent rises; ban letting fees; national landlord register; tackle homelessness.
- Keep household benefit cap (review regional levels); tailored back-to-work support; skills testing and mandatory training; pause/review Universal Credit; higher JSA for long contributors; abolish Bedroom Tax; reform Work Capability Assessment with disabled oversight.

Immigration, policing, justice
- +1,000 border staff funded by small charge on non-visa visitors; full exit checks; tighten short-term student visas; cap non-EU workers maintained.
- Ban overseas-only recruitment; extend Gangmasters Authority; English requirement for public-facing roles; two-year wait for EU migrants to claim benefits; end indefinite detention; protect vulnerable asylum seekers; support UN resettlement.
- Safeguard >10,000 police officers by structural reforms; neighbourhood policing guarantees; new Police Standards Authority; chartered officers; diversify recruitment.
- Anti-social behaviour payback; youth justice reform (18–20); ban “legal highs”; new child protection powers; prisons focused on rehabilitation; Victims’ Law.
- Violence against women and girls: new bill, commissioner, stable refuge funding; tighten gun licensing; widen legal aid; improve DNA retention rules.
- Extremism: stronger control measures; mandatory deradicalisation for returnees; updated investigatory powers with enhanced oversight; overhaul Prevent; tougher hate-crime laws.

Culture, sport, environment
- Creative education entitlement; free national museum entry maintained; more creative apprenticeships; PM’s committee on arts/creative industries; two hours school sport/week; supporter representation in football boards; 5% PL TV income to grassroots.
- Flood-prevention priority; local air-quality powers; forests in public ownership; strengthen wildlife/animal welfare; rural strategy; stronger supermarket watchdog.

Constitution, devolution, rights, media
- Constitutional Convention; replace House of Lords with elected Senate of Nations and Regions; votes at 16–17; repeal Lobbying Act; tougher lobbyist register; ban MPs’ paid directorships/consultancies; fair registration measures; party-donation caps.
- English Devolution Act: £30bn and powers to city/county regions; retain growth business rates; local Public Accounts Committees; community high-street powers incl. payday lenders/FOBTs.
- Scotland: implement Smith in full; further tax/welfare/job powers; maintain Barnett. Wales: reserved-powers model, Silk measures, funding floor. Northern Ireland: support shared future and economic pact.
- Require large firms to publish gender pay gap; strengthen maternity protections; race-equality strategy; advance LGBT rights; protect Human Rights Act/ECHR; extend FOI to private providers; media plurality rules; implement Leveson; keep Channel 4 public; support BBC value.

Foreign, defence, development, climate
- Multilateral approach; strong NATO/EU ties; criteria-led use of force; two-state solution; support Afghanistan; Asia taskforce; envoys for religious freedom and LGBT rights.
- Strategic Defence and Security Review; strengthen Armed Forces Covenant; Veterans’ Register; outlaw discrimination against service members; support defence industry; cyber-security requirements/reporting; maintain continuous at-sea nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament.
- Climate diplomacy: push for Paris deal with five-year ratchets, transparency, and net-zero in second half of century.
- Maintain 0.7% GNI on aid; focus on poorest/fragile states; Centre for Universal Health Coverage; reshape UN humanitarian system; support tax capacity in developing countries; tackle corruption and slavery in supply chains.
